mission.title: Packet Rider
mission.description: See the General's captured data home, then follow its packet headers to the corporation they point to.

npc.say: If you mean to test my patience, you won't have long to wait.
What are you doing here? Stop!
What are you doing here? Stop!

phase.briefing:
That despicable thief Mauser has jacked out of the simulation. Oh, well. We'll find his jack-in location sooner or later, I'm sure.
In other news from the outside, the General is heading home through the storm with his tail between his legs, and quite a few less Sentinels than he left with, thanks to those missile bombardments he ran into in the no-fly zone. Still, he--or, I should say, his Sentinels--did succeed in pulling some data out of the network they found out there. He's due to transmit the last of it shortly. Go see that it arrives safely, mm?

enter.say: The General's men have that place covered for his broadcast.

talk.say: Visibility is low, but the storm seems to be keeping the Machines off our backs. We're sending the last of the captured data now.

phase.briefing: Try not to lose that data, operative. It did come from the General, but despite appearances, it might actually be worth something.

enter.say: See the head technician, Weisbrod, about what to do with the data.

objective.text: Put the Data in the Computer

done.say: The data is extremely complex. We simply don't have the tools to process it effectively. Full comprehension could take...years.

Very good.
What? Hm... I wouldn't hope for a miracle decryption, but if you really must satisfy your curiosity, go ask Huang. She's just through there.

talk.say: Are you sure you kept that data free of contaminants? The analysis is picking up standard circa 1999 packet headers in there. That can't be right; the stuff we've seen from the foreign network so far has been of at least Machine-level complexity.

done.say: What? But those headers are ancient... The Machines only use those in simulated human networks inside the Matrix.
Let me ask you something: how many hack routines do you have loaded right now? Uh-huh... And you don't think those present a contamination risk?

near.say: Ah, more "Oligarch Network" data. Yes, just dump that in the computer over there.

phase.briefing:
For once, I think it was someone else screwing up instead of you, operative. Those network packets they found in the data point to a private corporate provider. Why they would be referenced in data flowing through an advanced network outside of the Matrix, I have no idea. So you'll just be paying them a visit to find out, won't you?
Hm... I suppose I should provide you with an escort to make sure you stay on task. Pick them up while we finish tracking those network addresses.

enter.say: Ookami should be in there with your reinforcements.

talk.say:
Whoever it is...has no business here. The Matrix is ours.
Take these with you and get out.

objective.text: Lead Bessel and Pigeon out of the area

near.say: Hmrrr... What can I do for you, little human?

phase.briefing:
It's a rented office of some sort, operative. You'll just have to go figure out who owns it.
Oh, we could probably find the information somewhere, but it would be more time-consuming and expensive than just sending you to kick the door in.
Just try to get the right address this time...

enter.say: That's supposed to be the spot. I'm getting some active readings.

near.say: Those are Ouroboros security guards! Does that mean the Ouroboros Corporation is involved in this?

mission.finish:
The Ouroboros Corporation? But why would that electronics company be mixed up with--
Bah, why am I speculating with you around, {player}? The echo always gets so annoying...
